Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

should verb

ought to: what is right or expected

also ought, ought to, shouldn’t, should have, oughtn’t, it won’t do to, it won’t do

classical

Cato Agr. 3.1: aedificāre diū cōgitāre oportet
Phaedr. 4.18.9: parce gaudēre oportet

oportet, oportēre, oportuit

verb, impersonal, with an infinitive, an accusative and infinitive, or a bare subjunctive

it is right, one should

What is fitting or to be expected. “Should have” is oportuit with the infinitive: cēnam jam esse coctam oportuit, dinner should have been cooked by now; mōrem gestum oportuit, you should have humoured him.

Other words

  • 1With an infinitive dēbeō speaks of a duty; for what simply has to be, Latin says necesse est. Lewis & Short: in classical prose always of moral necessity. Ruling: dēbeō is for duty.

    dēbeō1, dēbēre, dēbuī, dēbitum — ought, be bound to (a duty)

    verb, second conjugation, with an infinitive · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 28.1: animum dēbēs mūtāre, nōn caelum; Cic. Sen. 69: eō dēbet esse contentus; Traupman 355

    A duty owed: “you ought to”. Not for what is merely likely, nor for what has to be (see must).

  • nōn satis est (+ infinitive) — given for “it won’t do to”

    avoid · classical · Traupman 97, 305: it won’t do to (+ inf.), nōn satis est; Traupman 305

    Nōn satis est is “it is not enough” (nōn satis est ars sōla cocō, Mart. 14.220.1; see too little). For “it won’t do to …” say nōn oportet (above).

Examples

  • aedificāre diū cōgitāre oportet, cōnserere cōgitāre nōn oportet, sed facere oportet

    you should think long about building; about planting you shouldn’t think, you should just do itCato Agr. 3.1

  • properāte, cēnam jam esse coctam oportuit.

    Hurry up: dinner should have been cooked by now.Plaut. Cas. 765–766

  • Tua culpa. — Quid agerem? — Adulēscentī mōrem gestum oportuit.

    Your fault. — What was I to do? — You should have humoured the young man.Ter. Ad. 214–214c

  • parce gaudēre oportet et sēnsim querī

    one should rejoice sparingly and complain slowlyPhaedr. 4.18.9

  • animum dēbēs mūtāre, nōn caelum

    you ought to change your mind, not your skySen. Ep. 28.1

  • apēs, ut ajunt, dēbēmus imitārī

    we ought, as they say, to copy the beesSen. Ep. 84.3

See also must, be supposed to, shall, necessary, owe.
